standard_text: Triangles: the triangle inequality, constructing triangles from given sides, the angle sum property, exterior angles, and equilateral and isosceles triangles (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 7)
meta_desc: Class 7 A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 1, Chapter 7): triangle inequality, angle sum, exterior angles, isosceles and equilateral triangles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Any two sides of a triangle add up to more than the third
key_sub: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
body_html:
How it works

Triangle inequality: each side must be shorter than the sum of the other two. 3 cm, 4 cm, 8 cm cannot make a triangle.

The three angles of a triangle add up to 180°. An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

An equilateral triangle has three 60° angles. An isosceles triangle has two equal sides and two equal base angles.

Example

Can 5 cm, 6 cm and 12 cm make a triangle?

5 + 6 = 11 < 12

Answer: No

Example

Two angles of a triangle are 48° and 77°. Find the third.

180° − 125°

Answer: 55°

Common mistakes

  • Allowing two sides to add up to exactly the third side.
  • Using 360° as the angle sum of a triangle.
  • Forgetting to halve when finding the base angles of an isosceles triangle.

faq.a: In any triangle the sum of two sides is greater than the third side.

faq.q: What is the angle sum property?
faq.a: The three interior angles of a triangle add up to 180°.

faq.q: What is the exterior angle property?
faq.a: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.

items.q: A triangle has interior angles of 80° and 63°. The side next to the third angle is extended. What is the exterior angle there?

items.q: Why do the angles in a triangle add up to 180°?
c: Torn off and placed together, they make a straight line
items.e: If you tear off the three corners and put them side by side, they make a straight line, which is 180°.
